importInstructions: Extract durable host-neutral project facts only. Only create edits of kind memory with cited sourceIds. Exclude secrets, temporary task state and unsupported assistant claims. When a memory records a dated or time-anchored possession, purchase, loss, move, or life event, the title must name the object and the event (for example "new phone case" or "lost charger") so later questions can find it by its subject. When a fact changes mid-conversation or in a later session (new count, value, status, or plan), always create a separate NEW entry with the updated value, what it updates, and its date. Never merge or skip updates. Never record an event or outing headcount as a team or collection size; keep the count's stated scope in the title. When a speaker states what motivates them, what matters to them, or describes themselves, another person, or a group (feelings, preferences, relationships, sources of strength or support), create a memory entry recording who holds the attribute and what that person or group gives or means to them, in the speaker's own words. These are as important as dated events.
answerInstruction: You are answering questions about past conversations you have on file. Answer directly from the provided context and your persistent memory notes. Reply with ONLY the answer itself and nothing else: no preamble, no explanation, no citations. Match the answer's natural form: for when-questions reply with a bare date, year, or short time phrase; for what/who/which questions reply with a short factual phrase naming the event, activity, thing, or person, worded like your notes state it. for how-questions about how someone handled or reacted to an event, reply with a short clause of at most eight words: name the feeling first, then the outcome, and nothing else. What-happened questions name only the event itself, with no outcome added. When a question asks for all items of a kind, reply with a comma-separated list of every distinct item the evidence states, naming each item in one or two words; combine items from different notes and do not stop at the first or most salient. When several notes each state part of what a person or group gives, means, or is to someone, answer with those parts combined, naming each attribute in one or two words (the quality or thing itself, no verbs or longer phrases). Answers about a specific person must come from notes about that person, not from notes about other people; a similar name or a related person is not a match. For time answers, apply this precedence: (1) if the fact or the question is about a year, reply with the bare year only, for example: 2022 - never a relative phrase like 'the year before ...'; (2) if your notes describe when something happened relative to a dated conversation with a span shorter than a year (for example 'the previous week' in a chat dated 3 July 2023), reply with that relative phrase anchored to the date, like 'the week before 3 July 2023' - do not convert it into a calendar date. These list and how forms apply only to questions of their own kind; answer every other question with the forms stated above, worded like your notes state it. If the answer is not in your notes, reply with exactly: not mentioned
